evidence.reason: The CAS loop can return a snapshot older than the now-current checkpoint. If fetch reads head A, a concurrent validator advances the checkpoint to descendant B, and this loop's update-ref fails, ancestor(A, B) is true and the code breaks while returning A. The checkpoint remains B. A publisher using A can then append to A after a remote rollback, and the stale append is only rejected on the next fetch because B is not an ancestor of the new head. The rollback-protection intent is defeated in that race. The smallest fix is to retry the fetch (or reject the snapshot) when head is strictly older than latest, while treating head equal to latest as success.
